doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Sound, humanizing the saxophone, soprano and tenor
summary: Asked what he likes about his playing, Ries says he tries to make the instrument sound like his voice, thinking of trumpet on soprano.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: This has been a wonderful conversation, I’m really glad we could have it. I’m going to wrap up with an observation about your playing and then I’m going to put you on the spot for a moment. I particularly noticed your wonderful ability to play subtone really down at the bottom of the tenor. And then on the other hand when you played your soprano it was like ballsy. Because I hate when the soprano is played like you’re using one lung, that sort of like special — at any rate, I want to know what to wrap up, what do you like about your playing?

Wow that’s definitely putting me on the spot. Well I try — the first thing you hear from a person is their voice, right? I mean so whether you’re talking or singing or almost like — so you know the appealing nature of sounds, so I feel like okay the first thing you have is like the ability hopefully to translate — and I tell this to young musicians, I’ve had students over the years, talking about you are the instrument. Because the saxophone is just a piece of metal. You can put a different mouthpiece and different reed, of course everything makes a difference but it doesn’t do anything on its own. So I’m playing it so I’m the instrument. I’m breathing life into this piece of metal. So you know I guess what I try to do, and I attempt it, I don’t know if it’s what I like about my playing but I try, is to make it as much — is humanize the instrument as I can to make it not sound like an instrument so that it’s just my voice. That’s the idea and with the soprano and what you’re noticing when I play soprano I think about it as a trumpet more than the saxophone, because I started on trumpet and because my dad played the trumpet, and I even hold it straight out like a trumpet. So I’m more thinking about trumpet and singing than the saxophone. But having said that I also studied a lot of classical and I played in a saxophone quartet playing soprano so we were really doing a lot of string quartet kind of stuff so I really studied that a lot so that’s maybe that sound is I’m trying to be really focused on the sound of the soprano. The tenor was my first instrument so I end up thinking about you know the tenor sometimes is just like this beautiful like cello
